title: Render notices whose events carry several values

blocks.text: The operations notifier turns events into short notices. Each event names a template and carries one payload: a single value, an `Object[]` from the JSON decoder when the event has several values, or an `int[]` from the metrics feed. The notifier takes its renderer as a `BiFunction<String, Object, String>`, and until now it was configured with `String::format`. Notices with one value went out fine. The first event with two values failed with `MissingFormatArgumentException`, and the on-call engineer never heard about the cache that had restarted four times.

Finish `render(String template, Object payload)` in `src/main/java/practice/Notices.java`, which the notifier now uses as `Notices::render`. Each value of the payload fills the next format specifier of the template, whatever kind of payload the event carries. About three lines in total.

cases.says: a payload of one value fills the template's one specifier
an Object[] payload that arrives typed as Object still fills one specifier per element
an int[] payload fills one specifier per element, although an int[] is not an Object[]

origin.section: A Varargs Method Packs the Interface's Arguments, So an Array Becomes One Element

concepts: An int[] is never spread into a T... or Object... parameter, since it is not an Object[].
A varargs method used through a fixed-arity interface packs the interface's argument into a new array, so an Object[] passed as Object becomes one element.
